title: Structuring a Web App That Grows
description: Organise a small web app so adding the fifth feature is as easy as the first: a boilerplate trimmed to what the app actually needs, components extracted at the right moment instead of on principle, local state kept local until something genuinely needs to share it, routes added only when a screen earns its own URL, and a refactor timed to the third similar feature instead of the first or the tenth.

title: Integrating the Claude API Properly
description: Call an AI model from a web app without exposing keys or hanging the UI: keeping the key server-side behind a minimal proxy route, streaming a response into the UI as it arrives, handling a request that times out or needs a retry, and rate limiting your own endpoint before someone else's usage costs you money.

title: Styling and UX That Doesn't Fight the User
description: Style an app for clarity and low cognitive load, not decoration: establishing a clear visual hierarchy, defining a design system of five decisions instead of fifty ad hoc ones, treating loading and empty states as first-class screens, designing mobile-first for a phone in bed, and removing a step before styling it better.

title: Deploying and Managing Environments
description: Deploy a web app with separate environments and secrets handled correctly: shipping to Vercel end to end, scoping environment variables per environment instead of sharing one set, using preview deployments to catch bugs before they're live, rolling back a bad deploy in under a minute, and understanding what actually breaks when a custom domain is added.
